title: SecOps-NG Telemetry Binding
description: A telemetry binding declares an OCSF event class our content layer expects to consume or emit, and points to a sample payload that compilers and tests can validate against. SecOps-NG does NOT fork OCSF; we bind to upstream class UIDs and version, and join to the playbook, detection, and control layers via the shared `stable_id` shape.

stable_id.description: SecOps-NG stable identifier for this telemetry binding. Namespace convention: `telemetry.<slug>@v<semver>` — for example `telemetry.host_process_create@v1`. Same lexical shape as the playbook schema's stable_id so any layer can cross-reference any other.

content_version.description: Semantic version of this telemetry content artifact (independent of OCSF version).

summary.description: Operator-facing description of what this telemetry represents and where it originates.

ocsf.description: OCSF (Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework) class binding.

category_uid.description: OCSF category UID (e.g. 1 = System Activity, 2 = Findings, 3 = IAM, 4 = Network Activity, 6 = Application Activity).

class_uid.description: OCSF class UID (e.g. 1007 = Process Activity, 2001 = Security Finding).

class_name.description: Human-readable class name from the OCSF schema.

activity_id.description: Optional OCSF activity_id when this binding narrows the class to a single activity.

profiles.description: OCSF profiles overlaid on the event, e.g. ["cloud", "host"].

direction.description: Whether SecOps-NG content consumes events of this shape (ingest), produces them (emit), or both (typical for orchestrator hand-offs).

sample.description: Pointer to a canonical sample payload that conforms to the bound OCSF class. The payload is stored alongside this binding, not inline, to keep schema files small and reviewable.

path.description: Repo-relative path to the sample JSON payload, e.g. content-model/examples/telemetry.sample.json.

sha256.description: Optional integrity pin on the sample payload contents.

items.description: Dot-path into the OCSF event the content layer actually reads or writes, e.g. process.cmd_line, finding.uid.

fields_used.description: Subset of OCSF fields our content layer commits to. Lets reviewers reason about compatibility without diffing the whole OCSF schema.

detection_refs.description: Detection stable IDs that consume this telemetry. Joins to detection.schema.json#stable_id.

control_refs.description: Control stable IDs that draw attestation evidence from this telemetry. Joins to control.schema.json#stable_id.

playbook_refs.description: Playbooks (optionally specific CACAO step names) that read or emit this telemetry.

sources.description: Free-form provenance pointers — OCSF working-group notes, vendor schemas, advisories — that motivated this binding. Plain text only; no internal infra references.

stable_id.description: SecOps-NG stable identifier (shared shape across all content-model layers).
